players.product: ThinkSystem AI servers (Neptune liquid cooling) and AMD Helios racks

quarterly_data.signal: Group results, first quarter of fiscal 2026/27 (CEO Yuanqing Yang / CFO Winston Cheng): record revenue of $26.9 billion, up 43% year-on-year, the highest growth in five years; adjusted operating income up 141% to $1.5 billion and adjusted net income up 176% to $1.1 billion (above $1 billion for the first time), with adjusted operating and net margins of 5.7% and 4%. Reported net income was a loss of $609 million, mainly from a $1.7 billion non-cash fair value loss on warrant revaluation and $30 million of notional interest on convertible bonds. All three business groups set fiscal-Q1 revenue and operating-profit records; geographies grew 25% to 58%; R&D expenses rose 30% year-on-year.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $26.9 billion (+43% YoY); adjusted net income $1.1 billion (+176%); adjusted operating income $1.5 billion (+141%); reported net loss $609 million

quarterly_data.signal: AI-related revenue rose 60% year-on-year to over $9 billion and now accounts for 35% of group revenue (CEO and CFO).
quarterly_data.figure: AI-related revenue over $9 billion (+60% YoY), 35% of group revenue

quarterly_data.signal: Targets: CEO Yuanqing Yang said the goal set earlier this year of $100 billion revenue within two years is ahead of schedule: 'We are ready to deliver that in this fiscal year and driving to even higher profitability.' CFO Winston Cheng: Lenovo is 'on a strong path toward achieving a net income margin of over 5%', with ISG becoming a meaningful profit contributor and SSG's full ramp-up still to come.
quarterly_data.figure: $100 billion revenue target expected this fiscal year; net income margin target over 5%

quarterly_data.signal: Infrastructure Solutions Group (ISG): record revenue of $8.5 billion, up 98% year-on-year; record operating profit of $777 million and an all-time-high operating margin of 9.1%. Both CSP (cloud service provider) and E&SMB (enterprise and small & medium business) revenue nearly doubled year-on-year. Lenovo rose to number 2 in the global x86 server market; excluding international GPU sales in China in the prior year, global AI server revenue grew triple digits year-on-year, with broad strength across traditional compute, AI servers and storage. ISG President Ashley Gorakhpurwalla: the record margin is 'indicative of the performance of the business', not a one-time item - 'the growth was the story, not the mix' - though future mix dynamics will be driven by market and supply factors.
quarterly_data.figure: ISG revenue $8.5 billion (+98% YoY); operating profit $777 million; operating margin 9.1%

quarterly_data.signal: AI server pipeline expanded to $54 billion, up 157% quarter-on-quarter (more than doubling), on accelerating AI infrastructure momentum and a rapidly expanding customer base. ISG President Ashley Gorakhpurwalla: the pipeline is customer engagements, deals and future orders that are uncommitted or unqualified - Lenovo does not guide to committed orders or a conversion rate. Drivers named: agentic AI use cases in enterprises, private AI clouds becoming a standard approach for token efficiency, rising IT budgets with a higher AI mix, a strong server refresh cycle (one ThinkSystem server can replace six or seven older competitive boxes) and accelerating AI data center build-outs.
quarterly_data.figure: AI server pipeline $54 billion (+157% QoQ), uncommitted

quarterly_data.signal: NVIDIA platform roadmap: CFO Winston Cheng said Lenovo is scaling GB300 deployments while accelerating Vera Rubin rack solution readiness and time to market, through deepened partnerships with NVIDIA, AMD and Intel. ISG President Ashley Gorakhpurwalla: Lenovo is 'fully supporting with supply readiness' the NVIDIA and Lenovo platforms around B200, sees 'very strong demand' for Lenovo NVIDIA B300 and NVIDIA GB300 solutions (air-cooled or direct liquid cooling), and is 'building a very robust pipeline for our Vera Rubin roadmap' from enterprise agentic use cases to hyperscale AI cloud deployments; based on Lenovo's testing and pilots, he called the architecture 'a generational leap'. Lenovo Neptune liquid cooling is now in generation 6.

Customer wins (unnamed, CFO): in CSP, Lenovo delivered an AI factory with over 7,000 GPUs for a leading AI cloud provider and supported another AI infrastructure provider's expansion with the deployment of thousands of servers; with Neptune liquid cooling it delivered high-density AI factory solutions with 18.3 exaFLOPS of performance.
quarterly_data.figure: AI factory with over 7,000 GPUs; 18.3 exaFLOPS

quarterly_data.signal: Manufacturing capacity: Lenovo expanded its North Carolina smart campus, adding meaningful new server manufacturing capacity to capture rising demand from hyperscalers and enterprise customers (CFO).

Memory and component supply (CEO Yuanqing Yang): 'we believe demand for memory will continue to rise for a considerable period ahead, at least by the end of next year. That means that the supply will be still constrained.' He said Lenovo is now among the top customers of the major semiconductor suppliers, sources from suppliers in the U.S., Korea and China ('we definitely cannot ignore the China supply'), and can adjust front-end pricing in a timely manner when material costs rise. IDG President Luca Rossi: an inflationary cost environment, 'particularly in certain commodity memory, but memory is not the only one'.
quarterly_data.figure: memory supply constrained at least through the end of next year (CEO view)

quarterly_data.signal: Storage: Infinidat is now part of Lenovo Group; CFO Winston Cheng said the storage acquisition added a $38 billion TAM. ISG President Ashley Gorakhpurwalla: the storage business has 'a markedly higher margin profile' that will start to enter the ISG mix, and Lenovo is getting more visibility into a pipeline of mission-critical storage expansion across verticals up to AI data centers.
quarterly_data.figure: storage acquisition added a $38 billion TAM

quarterly_data.signal: Intelligent Devices Group (IDG): record fiscal-Q1 revenue of $17.1 billion, up 27% year-on-year; operating profit up 27% to $1.2 billion at a 7.1% operating margin. Global PC market share reached 24.2%, gaining share for the 12th consecutive quarter and extending the lead over the number 2 player for the 10th consecutive quarter by more than 5 points; record AI PC global market share of 25.1%. Tablet revenue rose more than 80% year-on-year; smartphone revenue rose 15%, Motorola posting its highest first-quarter revenue since 2015 with a record 37% premium revenue mix.
quarterly_data.figure: IDG revenue $17.1 billion (+27% YoY); operating margin 7.1%; PC share 24.2%; AI PC share 25.1%

quarterly_data.signal: Device market outlook (IDG President Luca Rossi): Q1 PC demand was stronger than expected, partly from demand pulled ahead of future cost increases and from AI PC adoption. For the second half of the fiscal year Lenovo expects the PC market to contract double digits in units, 'probably around 15%', with commercial more resilient than consumer, and the smartphone market to decline around 20% on the inflationary cost environment. Lenovo intends to keep gaining share and to offset unit declines with higher ASP, premium and AI PC mix while maintaining industry-leading profitability; for Motorola it expects to more than offset the unit decline with higher ASP and premium mix, with a further premium-mix enhancement in late 2026 and 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: H2 PC market units down around 15%; smartphone market down around 20% (company estimates)

quarterly_data.signal: Solutions and Services Group (SSG): record revenue of $2.9 billion, up 28% year-on-year, the 21st consecutive quarter of double-digit growth; operating profit up 39% to $697 million at a record 24.2% operating margin. AI services revenue grew triple digits; managed services plus projects and solutions reached a record 62.4% of SSG revenue; Lenovo TruScale grew 35%, with TruScale Infrastructure-as-a-Service bookings in 'hypergrowth' on AI factory wins; projects and solutions are supported by a multi-quarter booking backlog. CFO: AI adds over $200 billion of incremental opportunity this fiscal year, and Lenovo expects total SSG TAM to grow to more than $850 billion by fiscal 2029/30.
quarterly_data.figure: SSG revenue $2.9 billion (+28% YoY); operating profit $697 million; operating margin 24.2%
